"'''Bennie and the Jets'''" (also titled "'''Benny & the Jets'''") is a song written by British musician [[Elton John]] and lyricist [[Bernie Taupin]], and performed by John.<ref>{{cite web |last=Janovitz |first=Bill |title=Bennie & the Jets – Elton John | Song Info |url=http://www.allmusic.com/song/bennie-the-jets-mt0009263845 |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref> The song first appeared on the ''[[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road]]'' album in 1973. "Bennie and the Jets" has been one of John's most popular songs and was performed during his appearance at [[Live Aid]].

The track was a massive hit in the United States and Canada, released in 1974 as an A-side using the spelling "Bennie". In most territories the track was released as the B-side of "[[Candle in the Wind]]", using the spelling "Benny". Album artwork (back-cover track listing and center-panel design) consistently lists the song as "Bennie" while either "Bennie" or "Benny" appears on the vinyl album depending on territory. The track was released as an A-side in the UK in 1976, as "Benny and the Jets".

It is ranked number 371 on ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s list of [[The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Bennie and the Jets ranked #371 on Rolling Stone 500 Greatest Songs List |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-songs-of-all-time-1224767/elton-john-bennie-and-the-jets-1224967/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=15 September 2021 |access-date=24 September 2021}}</ref>

"Bennie and the Jets" (also titled "Benny & the Jets") is a song written by British musician Elton John and lyricist Bernie Taupin, and performed by John. The song first appeared on the Goodbye Yellow Brick Road album in 1973. "Bennie and the Jets" has been one of John's most popular songs and was performed during his appearance at Live Aid.

The track was a massive hit in the United States and Canada, released in 1974 as an A-side using the spelling "Bennie". In most territories the track was released as the B-side of "Candle in the Wind", using the spelling "Benny". Album artwork (back-cover track listing and center-panel design) consistently lists the song as "Bennie" while either "Bennie" or "Benny" appears on the vinyl album depending on territory. The track was released as an A-side in the UK in 1976, as "Benny and the Jets".

It is ranked number 371 on Rolling Stone{{'}}s list of The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time.

sections.heading: Song composition
sections.wikitext:
The song tells of "Bennie and the Jets", a fictional band of whom the song's narrator is a fan. In a 2014 ''Rolling Stone'' interview, Taupin said, "I saw Bennie and the Jets as a sort of proto-sci-fi punk band, fronted by an androgynous woman, who looks like something out of a [[Helmut Newton]] photograph."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Greene |first=Andy |date=14 March 2014 |title=Elton John & Bernie Taupin on 'Goodbye Yellow Brick Road' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/elton-john-and-bernie-taupin-look-back-at-goodbye-yellow-brick-road-205112/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref>

Produced by [[Gus Dudgeon]], the song was recorded during the ''Goodbye Yellow Brick Road'' sessions in France at [[Château d'Hérouville]]'s Strawberry Studios,<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.wnew.com/2008/08/video-classi-12.html |title=Goodbye Yellow Brick Road at |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |date=19 August 2008 |access-date=26 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091120200821/http://www.wnew.com/2008/08/video-classi-12.html |archive-date=20 November 2009}}</ref> where John and Taupin had recorded their previous two albums ''[[Honky Château]]'' and ''[[Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player]]''.

When performing the song live, John rarely plays the studio arrangement, and often makes subtle or even drastic changes, sometimes including phrases from Glenn Miller's "[[In the Mood]]" and closing with the five-note combination from John Williams's score for ''[[Close Encounters of the Third Kind]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bBMWwU3Yy1s |title=Elton John – Bennie and the Jets (Live at Hammersmith Odeon in 1982) |website=[[YouTube]] |date=11 October 2012}}</ref>{{bcn|date=December 2022}} During his live performances, the piano solo has been played in all sorts of variations, from very close to the original to wildly improvised and extended versions, such as the elaborate version during his [[Central Park]] concert in 1980, the version from his 30 June 1984 Wembley Stadium performance and another take on it during the "Elton and his band" part of [[Live in Australia with the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra|the show recorded in Sydney, Australia, on 14 December 1986]], his last show before his throat surgery in January 1987.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1987/01/07/Pop-music-star-Elton-John-does-not-have-throat/7825536994000/ |title=Pop music star Elton John does not have throat}}</ref>
sections.text:
The song tells of "Bennie and the Jets", a fictional band of whom the song's narrator is a fan. In a 2014 Rolling Stone interview, Taupin said, "I saw Bennie and the Jets as a sort of proto-sci-fi punk band, fronted by an androgynous woman, who looks like something out of a Helmut Newton photograph."

Produced by Gus Dudgeon, the song was recorded during the Goodbye Yellow Brick Road sessions in France at Château d'Hérouville's Strawberry Studios, where John and Taupin had recorded their previous two albums Honky Château and Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player.

When performing the song live, John rarely plays the studio arrangement, and often makes subtle or even drastic changes, sometimes including phrases from Glenn Miller's "In the Mood" and closing with the five-note combination from John Williams's score for Close Encounters of the Third Kind.{{bcn|date=December 2022}} During his live performances, the piano solo has been played in all sorts of variations, from very close to the original to wildly improvised and extended versions, such as the elaborate version during his Central Park concert in 1980, the version from his 30 June 1984 Wembley Stadium performance and another take on it during the "Elton and his band" part of the show recorded in Sydney, Australia, on 14 December 1986, his last show before his throat surgery in January 1987.

sections.heading: Production
North American single release
sections.wikitext:
The song was the closing track on side one of the double album ''[[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road]]'', and John was set against releasing it as a single, believing it would fail. [[CKLW]] in [[Windsor, Ontario]], began heavy airplay of the song and it became the No. 1 song in the Detroit market.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bliss |first=Karen |title=The Legacy of Rosalie Trombley, Radio Pioneer Immortalized in Bob Seger's 'Rosalie' and Breaker of 'Bennie and the Jets' | Billboard |url=https://www.readability.com/articles/qdowbsdy |website=Readability.com |date=21 January 2016 |access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref> This attention caused other American and Canadian Top 40 stations to add it to their playlists as well. As a result, the song peaked at No. 1 on the US singles chart in 1974. In the US, it was [[Music recording certification|certified]] Gold on 8 April 1974 and Platinum on 13 September 1995 by the RIAA,<ref>{{cite certification |region=United States |type=single |artist=John, Elton |title=Bennie _ the Jets |access-date=2 July 2012}}</ref> and had sold 2.8 million copies by August 1976.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Jahr |first=Cliff |title=Elton John, Lonely at the Top: Rolling Stone's 1976 Cover Story |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/elton-john-lonely-at-the-top-rolling-stones-1976-cover-story-20110202?page=2 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone (magazine)|Rolling Stone]] |date=2 February 2011 |access-date=2 July 2012}}</ref>

''[[Cash Box]]'' said that "the song is a strong one and worth every second of its 5:10."<ref name=cb>{{cite news|title=CashBox Record Reviews|date=16 February 1974|page=30|accessdate=2021-12-11|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1974/CB-1974-02-16.pdf|newspaper=Cash Box}}</ref> ''[[Record World]]'' said that "With Elton showcasing his remarkable voice range, it can't miss grabbing the top spot."<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine |title=Hits of the Week |url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/74/RW-1974-02-16.pdf |magazine=Record World |date=16 February 1974 |page=1 |access-date=17 March 2023}}</ref>

"Bennie and the Jets" was John's first Top 40 hit on what at the time was called the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|''Billboard'' Hot Soul Singles]] chart, where it peaked at No. 15, the highest position out of the three of his singles which reached that chart.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elton John: Charts and Awards |url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/elton-john-mn0000796734/awards |publisher=AllMusic |access-date=21 August 2013}}</ref> The acceptance of "Bennie" on R&B radio helped land John, a huge soul music fan, a guest appearance on the 17 May 1975 edition of ''[[Soul Train]]'', where he played "Bennie and the Jets" and "[[Philadelphia Freedom (song)|Philadelphia Freedom]]". In Canada, it held the No. 1 spot on the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' national singles chart for two weeks (13–20 April), becoming his first No. 1 single of 1974 and his fourth overall.<ref>{{cite web |title=Item Display – RPM – Library and Archives Canada |url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/rpm/028020-119.01-e.php?brws_s=1&file_num=nlc008388.5006a&type=1&interval=24&PHPSESSID=ccntousk30frf6h4jsn237nm12 |url-status=dead |publisher=Collectionscanada.gc.ca |access-date=26 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020114305/http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/rpm/028020-119.01-e.php?brws_s=1&file_num=nlc008388.5006a&type=1&interval=24&PHPSESSID=ccntousk30frf6h4jsn237nm12 |archive-date=20 October 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Item Display – RPM – Library and Archives Canada |url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/rpm/028020-119.01-e.php?brws_s=1&file_num=nlc008388.5033a&type=1&interval=24&PHPSESSID=ccntousk30frf6h4jsn237nm12 |url-status=dead |publisher=Collectionscanada.gc.ca |access-date=26 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020114345/http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/rpm/028020-119.01-e.php?brws_s=1&file_num=nlc008388.5033a&type=1&interval=24&PHPSESSID=ccntousk30frf6h4jsn237nm12 |archive-date=20 October 2012}}</ref>
sections.text:
The song was the closing track on side one of the double album Goodbye Yellow Brick Road, and John was set against releasing it as a single, believing it would fail. CKLW in Windsor, Ontario, began heavy airplay of the song and it became the No. 1 song in the Detroit market. This attention caused other American and Canadian Top 40 stations to add it to their playlists as well. As a result, the song peaked at No. 1 on the US singles chart in 1974. In the US, it was certified Gold on 8 April 1974 and Platinum on 13 September 1995 by the RIAA, and had sold 2.8 million copies by August 1976.

Cash Box said that "the song is a strong one and worth every second of its 5:10." Record World said that "With Elton showcasing his remarkable voice range, it can't miss grabbing the top spot."

"Bennie and the Jets" was John's first Top 40 hit on what at the time was called the Billboard Hot Soul Singles chart, where it peaked at No. 15, the highest position out of the three of his singles which reached that chart. The acceptance of "Bennie" on R&B radio helped land John, a huge soul music fan, a guest appearance on the 17 May 1975 edition of Soul Train, where he played "Bennie and the Jets" and "Philadelphia Freedom". In Canada, it held the No. 1 spot on the RPM national singles chart for two weeks (13–20 April), becoming his first No. 1 single of 1974 and his fourth overall.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: In May 2017, the music video for "Bennie and the Jets" premiered at the [[Cannes Film Festival]] as a winner of ''Elton John: The Cut'', a competition organised in partnership with [[AKQA]], Pulse Films, and YouTube in honour of the fiftieth anniversary of his songwriting relationship with [[Bernie Taupin]]. The competition called upon independent filmmakers to submit [[Film treatment|treatments]] for music videos for one of three Elton John songs from the 1970s, with each song falling within a specific concept category. "Bennie and the Jets" was designated for the choreography category, and was directed by Jack Whiteley and Laura Brownhill. The video was influenced by early cinema and the work of [[Busby Berkeley]], portraying characters as participants on a talent show auditioning for Bennie.<ref name="people-eltonjohnthecut">{{cite web|title=WATCH: Elton John and Bernie Taupin's 'Tiny Dancer,' 'Rocket Man' and 'Bennie and the Jets' Just Got New Music Videos|url=http://people.com/music/elton-john-tiny-dancer-rocket-man-bennie-and-the-jets-music-videos-the-cut/|website=People|access-date=26 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Elton John Premieres Three Music Videos for His '70s Classics|url=http://www.out.com/music/2017/5/25/elton-john-premieres-three-music-videos-his-70s-classics|website=Out Magazine|date=25 May 2017 |access-date=26 May 2017}}</ref>

sections.wikitext:
* The [[Beastie Boys]] released a cover of this song on their ''[[Beastie Boys Anthology: The Sounds of Science|The Sounds of Science]]'' album in 1999.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sammerch.com/product/478/BB_Anthology_The_Sounds_Of_Science_Book_&_CD_Set |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080502070237/http://www.sammerch.com/product/478/BB_Anthology_The_Sounds_Of_Science_Book_%26_CD_Set |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 May 2008 |title=The Sounds of Science at Beastie Boys store |publisher=Sammerch.com |access-date=26 May 2011 }}</ref> The song, titled "Benny and the Jets", was sung by frequent Beastie Boys collaborator [[Biz Markie]], who often mumbles the words while singing. This recording was first released in 1995 as a [[flexi disc]] inside of issue two of the Beastie Boys' ''[[Grand Royal]]'' magazine.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dearmore |first=Kelly |url=http://www.dallasobserver.com/1998-05-28/music/he-got-game/ |title=He got game – Page 1 – Music – Dallas |newspaper=Dallas Observer |date=28 May 1998 |access-date=26 May 2011 |archive-date=17 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617065123/http://www.dallasobserver.com/1998-05-28/music/he-got-game/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

* [[Ben Folds]] riffed on both the title and the piano sounds for his song ''Hiroshima (B B B Benny Hit His Head)'' off of the 2008 album [[Way To Normal]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Aaron |first1=S. Victor |title=Ben Folds’ Way to Normal pointed the way back to a few %*@#-ing Five-era successes |url=https://somethingelsereviews.com/2015/09/25/ben-folds-way-to-normal/ |website=somethingelsereviews.com |access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref>

Thank You 4 Your Service]]''. John, Busta Rhymes and Jack White are  given feature credits on the track.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whosampled.com/cover/261889/Miguel-Wale-Bennie-and-the-Jets-Elton-John-Bennie-and-the-Jets/|title=Miguel feat. Wale cover of Elton John's 'Bennie and the Jets' | WhoSampled|website=[[WhoSampled]] }}</ref>

Blige album)|Mary]]'').<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/Mrk4uJHW-Ec |title=Mary J. Blige – Deep Inside |via=YouTube |date=16 June 2009 |access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref> Because of the extensive use of the piano parts, both Elton John and Bernie Taupin are credited as co-writers of "Deep Inside". * [[Miguel (singer)|Miguel]] and rapper [[Wale (rapper)|Wale]] recorded a cover of the song for the 2014 reissue of the ''Goodbye Yellow Brick Road'' album. It really makes the best of what the song is all about."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Weber |first1=Lindsey |title=Hear Miguel's 'Bennie and the Jets' Cover |url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/03/hear-miguels-bennie-and-the-jets-cover.html |website=[[New York (magazine)#Vulture|Vulture]] |access-date=8 September 2021 |date=21 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Newman |first1=Jason |title=Elton John Talks Miguel and Wale's 'Bennie and the Jets' Cover |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/elton-john-talks-miguel-and-wales-bennie-and-the-jets-cover-243457/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=8 September 2021 |date=21 March 2014}}</ref>

The audition was controversial due to comments made by [[Katy Perry]] that were called "Mom Shaming". Liebe eventually left the show. On 6 May 2023, Liebe released a fully produced cover version of "Bennie and The Jets" with producer [[Fernando Perdomo]] providing all instrumentation.{{fact|date=May 2024}}

*[[The Fearless Flyers]] produced an instrumental cover named "Kenni and the Jets" on their 2020 album ''Tailwinds''.
* The song was also featured on the soundtrack to the 1998 movie ''[[Sliding Doors]]'' and the 2006 film ''[[Running with Scissors (film)|Running With Scissors]]''..
* In 2025 [[Joy Crookes]] "unintentionally"<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Geraghty |first1=Hollie |title=Rediscovering Joy: How Joy Crookes Made Her Return with Resilient New Album 'Juniper' |url=https://www.rollingstone.co.uk/music/features/joy-crookes-interview-juniper-photos-53799/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone|Rolling Stone UK]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]] |access-date=5 October 2025 |date=16 September 2025}}</ref> used elements from "Bennie and the Jets" for the third song of her album ''[[Juniper (Joy Crookes album)|Juniper]]'' that is called ''Carmen''. According to the artist it is about "unrealistic beauty standards, and how they’re kicking all our arses" and Elton John "was super supportive about it, and really loves the song". Nevertheless Elton John and Bernie Taupin were honoured at the release with credits as writers.

This recording was first released in 1995 as a flexi disc inside of issue two of the Beastie Boys' Grand Royal magazine.

sections.heading: Mondegreens in the song
sections.wikitext: The song contains the line "She's got electric boots, a [[mohair]] suit", which is often misheard as "She's got electric [[breast|boobs]], and mohair shoes".<ref>{{cite web|first=Lawrence |last=DiStasi |url=http://distasiblog.blogspot.com/2011/07/mondegreens.html |title=DiStasiblog: Mondegreens |website=Distasiblog.blogspot.com |date=29 July 2011 |access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref> A scene in the film ''[[27 Dresses]]'' shows that this is but one of many [[mondegreen]]s that listeners have invented for this song.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vulture.com/2018/01/celebrating-a-decade-of-27-dresses-and-bennie-and-the-jets.html|work=Vulture|date=12 January 2018|title=Celebrating 10 Years of 27 Dresses' Insane, Iconic 'Bennie and the Jets' Scene |quote=It's the perfect 'drunken rom-com scene' song, because it's okay to sing the wrong words to this song; who even knows what the right words are?}}</ref>
sections.text: The song contains the line "She's got electric boots, a mohair suit", which is often misheard as "She's got electric boobs, and mohair shoes". A scene in the film 27 Dresses shows that this is but one of many mondegreens that listeners have invented for this song.
